source.name: CPIC
source.guidelineName: CYP2D6, CYP2C19, CYP2B6, SLC6A4, HTR2A and Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor Antidepressants

records.cpicRecommendationVerbatim: Consider a clinically appropriate alternative antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19. If citalopram or escitalopram are clinically appropriate, and adequate efficacy is not achieved at standard maintenance dosing, consider titrating to a higher maintenance dose.

cpicImplicationsVerbatim.CYP2C19: Increased metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 rapid and normal metabolizers. Lower plasma concentrations decrease the probability of clinical benefit.

records.cpicCommentsVerbatim: Drug-drug interactions and other patient characteristics (e.g., age, renal function, liver function) should be considered when adjusting dose or selecting an alternative therapy.
records.patientText: Your CYP2C19 result may affect how your body handles escitalopram. Discuss the result with your prescriber or pharmacist.

records.cpicRecommendationVerbatim: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose. If patient does not adequately respond to recommended maintenance dosing, consider titrating to a higher maintenance dose or switching to a clinically appropriate alternative antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19.

cpicImplicationsVerbatim.CYP2C19: Increase in metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 normal metabolizers. Lower plasma concentrations decrease the probability of clinical benefit.

records.cpicRecommendationVerbatim: Initiate therapy with recommended starting dose. Consider a slower titration schedule and lower maintenance dose than normal metabolizers.

cpicImplicationsVerbatim.CYP2C19: Reduced metabolism when compared to CYP2C19 normal metabolizers. Higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.

records.cpicRecommendationVerbatim: Consider a clinically appropriate antidepressant not predominantly metabolized by CYP2C19. If citalopram or escitalopram are clinically appropriate, consider a lower starting dose, slower titration schedule and 50% reduction of the standard maintenance dose as compared to normal metabolizers.

cpicImplicationsVerbatim.CYP2C19: Reduced metabolism of citalopram and escitalopram to less active compounds when compared to CYP2C19 normal and intermediate metabolizers. Higher plasma concentrations may increase the probability of side effects.

records.cpicCommentsVerbatim: Per the FDA warning, citalopram 20 mg/day is the maximum recommended dose in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers due to the risk of QT prolongation. FDA product labeling additionally cautions that citalopram dose should be limited to 20 mg/day in patients with hepatic impairment, those taking a CYP2C19 inhibitor, and patients greater than 60 years of age.
